title.narrative: Safety Net Systems for the Poorest

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve the equity, efficiency, transparency and shock-responsiveness of major safety net programs to benefit the poorest and most vulnerable households.

The objective of the Safety Net Systems for the Poorest Project for Bangladesh is to improve the equity, efficiency and transparency of major social safety net programs to benefit the poorest households. The proposed project includes three components: (i) support to five safety net programs by financing a portion of program costs in line with progress against a set of Disbursement Linked Indicators; (ii) strengthening of Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief (MoDMR) program administration and transparency; and (iii) development of the Bangladesh Poverty Database. The first component will reimburse the Government of Bangladesh for results, while the other two components will be seen as a financing instrument for the inputs needed to achieve the results under first component. Second and third components will finance all inputs such as personnel, design of IT systems as well as hardware, monitoring systems, vehicles and other equipment, consultants, and incremental operating costs.

title.narrative: Increase use of efficient administrative systems

comment.narrative: This was a DLI and the end target was fully achieved and the corresponding funds were disbursed by June 2019. This indicator pertains to the development and operationalization of MoDMR/DDM Safety Nets MIS which was facing delays. Hence, the DLI framework and associated result indicators were modified and two new targets were added for FY 2018 and FY 2019. The project achieved the revised targets in time and all DLI values were disbuursed by June 2019.

title.narrative: Establishment of Data Center and Disaster Recovery Sites

comment.narrative: The indicator target was achieved at project closing. While the data center was established by FY 2018, it took until FY 2021 to become functional due to delays in completing the MoU between DDM/MoDMR and BBS. However, MoDMR/DDM was unable to establish the disaster recovery site due to delays in completing discussions with Bangladesh Computer Council (expected service provider). Moreover, there was hardware failure in the data center - identified in FY 2023. This to DDM migrating its MIS to the National Data Center operated by Bangladesh Data Center Company Limited (BDCCL) in 2024. The BDCCL National Data Center which currently hosts the DDM Consolidated MIS is a tier 4 data center which has a dedicated disaster recovery site.

comment.narrative: End target was surpassed by June 2017. The indicator was not tracked beyond FY 2019 as the project did not co-finance these programs.

The inicator target was not achieved at project closing. In fact, the MIS development was only completed in December 2024 and hence, there was no time left to train DDM personnel on MIS usage. This activity will be carried forward and completed under the ISO project.

The indicator was partially achieved at closing. The indicator was introduced in FY 2020 through AF2 with an end target of 990,000 beneficiaries. But In FY 2022 Government of Bangladesh doubled the wage rate for the EGPP within the same budget envelope as the preceding five fiscal years. The program wage rate change was made to keep up with the increasing day laborer market wage rates, to retain the program's self-selection characteristic, while concurrently reducing focus on areas with lower levels of poverty. This meant a halving of the beneficiary coverage nationally while the geographic focus shifted only to the highest poverty upazilas. However, the total coverage (achievement) was still 20% short of the end target.

title.narrative: Workdays provided under Rohingya community services/works

comment.narrative: The indicator target was surpassed at project close (more than 200% of the end target).

The project achieved only 59 percent of its end target under this indicator despite surpassing the beneficiary coverage target for EGPP+. The reason behind this is the delays in the implementation of sub-projects caused by delays in government budget allocation. These delays essentially meant, no beneficiary completed all his / her available wordays in any given year.
This target was achieved at program close. However, it did not have the desired impact because of NHD development remaining incomplete.

This target was achieved by December 2023 (123,499 beneficiaries) and surpassed at project closing. The beneficiary numbers comprise of EGPP+ beneficiaries in Cox's Bazar, Jamalpur, Netrokona, Gaibandha, Kurigram and Sunamganj districts. It is important to note that the original end target (AF2) was 40,000 (only Cox's Bazar) which was increased to 100,000 through the 5th restructuring considering the roll-out of EGPP+ in 5 new districts during FY2023.

The indicator's end target was surpassed in June 2023 and coverage increased even further (227 percent of end the target) at closing. The indicator was introduced during AF2 in FY2020 but there was very little progress till December 2022 due to implementation delays caused by COVID 19.
